quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in one part of the lane and never move from that spot.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Ride only in the center of the lane so other drivers can see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so other drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as needed based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane offer a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane provides three paths: the left side, the center, and the right side.

questions.question: When riding, the best protection for a rider is:

options.text: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
A good understanding of motorcycle laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid crashes is to keep distance from other vehicles. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Wearing proper safety gear is also important.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it signals a right turn or right lane change.

questions.question: Linked and integrated braking systems:

options.text: Connect the front and rear brakes.
Should be avoided because they reduce rider control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Linked braking systems apply both brakes when you use either one. Integrated braking systems apply some front braking whenever the rear brake is used. Both systems make sure you use both brakes when stopping.

questions.question: Studies show that most riders involved in crashes:

options.text: Do not brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.
Brake the front tire too hard and do not brake the rear tire hard enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes do not brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter so the brake applies when you downshift.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes receive pressure. Check your owner's manual to learn how your motorcycle's braking system works.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends the right leg, it signals that there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: To swerve correctly:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of your turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side where you want to turn. After you avoid the hazard, press the opposite handgrip to go back to your original direction.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person who is age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person of legal drinking age with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it calmly. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: A child passenger should:

options.text: Sit in front of the rider.
Not need to reach the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit behind the rider.
questions.explanation: A child should always sit directly behind the rider. A child in front may not balance well and could block the rider's control of the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up less space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is less likely to get separated.
A close group gets to the destination faster than a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: A close group gets to the destination faster than a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close group uses less road space, is easier to see, and stays together better at traffic lights. However, a close group does not arrive faster than a spread-out group.

questions.question: Do not change gears on railroad tracks because:

options.text: Other drivers may not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface makes shifting difficult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears on railroad tracks because your motorcycle might stall while crossing them.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you from behind, you should:

options.text: Move to the center of your lane.
Move to the left side of your lane.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Stay wherever you are in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This reduces the risk of a collision with the passing vehicle.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: You should shift to a higher gear:

options.text: Before the engine reaches its maximum recommended speed.
After the engine reaches its maximum recommended speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the engine reaches its maximum recommended speed.
questions.explanation: Shift to a higher gear before the engine RPM reaches maximum speed. Shift soon enough to avoid over-revving the engine, but not so soon that the engine struggles.

questions.question: When loading cargo on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Avoid placing items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Load heavier items in front of the tank bag and over or in front of the rear axle. Placing cargo behind the rear axle may reduce your control.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride in the left side of your lane.
Ride in the right side of your lane.
Ride in any part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. This discourages the other driver from returning to your lane too early.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they often appear to be:

options.text: Traveling faster than they actually are.
Traveling slower than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Due to their small size, motorcycles may appear to be traveling faster than they actually are.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Put inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Keep safe distance and not tailgate other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep safe distance and not tailgate other riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. Check your mirrors often to see riders behind you. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Keep proper space between all riders in the group.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. If you bend your left arm at the elbow and point it downward, you are signaling that you plan to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge where the vehicle is and how fast it is going.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: You can see the roadway through vehicles in front of you.
The weather is clear and pleasant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is heavy.
questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is usually enough, but increase it when you need more time to stop. This includes heavy traffic, bad weather, nighttime, when you cannot see ahead, or when the road is slippery.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green clothing makes you more visible. Dark or dull colors do not work as well.
